Retrieved 25 April 2022. is a species of the [[Begoniaceae]] that is native to [[South America]]n countries of [[Argentina]], [[Brazil]], [[Paraguay]], and [[Uruguay]].[http://tropical.theferns.info/viewtropical.php?id=Begonia+cucullata Begonia cucullata] A common garden plant and part of the section ''[[Begonia]]'', it was described in 1805 by [[Carl Ludwig Willdenow]] (1765–1812). The specific epithet "cucullata" means "resembling a hood" or "hooded".[https://plants.ifas.ufl.edu/plant-directory/begonia-cucullata/ Begonia cucullata] ==Description== The plant is an upright growing, [[herbaceous]] [[perennial plant|perennial]] that has almost symmetrical succulent pale green to pale reddish brown leaves that are ovate, [[glabrousness (botany)|glabrous]] 4–8 cm long and 6 cm wide, with edged, glossy and toothed [[crenation]].''database, NODC Taxonomic Code'', 1996 Grown as a [[groundcover]], the flowers of the plant are red, pink or white that bloom in the summer or year-round in warmer places, and the fruits have three wings.[https://worldoffloweringplants.com/begonia-cucullata-wax-begonia/ Begonia cucullata – Wax Begonia ]{{Cite web |url=https://www.itis.gov/servlet/SingleRpt/SingleRpt?search_topic=TSN&search_value=22330#null |title=Begonia cucullata Willd. |website=siit.conabio.gob.mx (Mexico) ITIS Regional: The Integrated Taxonomic Information System |access-date=June 5, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170429125543/http://www.itis.gov/#null |archive-date=April 29, 2017 |url-status=live }} ==Range== Native to South America, wax begonia is also found growing [[invasive species|invasively]] in [[Florida]], namely from the northern and central peninsula west to central panhandle, and also in [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]]. The plant may invade waysides, deforested areas, overgrazed pastureland, and wastelands.''Begoniaceae of North America Update'' Because they are such prolific seed producers, seeds are thought to be the primary way begonias spread when left unchecked. They can also root very easily, but this may not play much of a role under natural conditions.{{cite web |url=https://plants.ifas.ufl.edu/plant-directory/begonia-cucullata/ |title=Begonia cucullata |date=n.d. |website=Center for Aquatic and Invasive Plants |publisher=University of Florida Institute of Food and Agricultural Sciences |access-date=8 Feb 2021}} ==Cultivation== Older varieties prefer shade, though newer varieties tolerate both full sun and shade. Indoors, they can thrive in a south- or east-facing window, provided they are acclimated when their environment is changed.Langeland, K.A. and K. Craddock Burks. 1998. Identification and Biology of Non-Native Plants in Florida’s Natural Areas. IFAS Publication SP 257. University of Florida, Gainesville. 165 pp. ==Varieties== ''Begonia × semperflorens-cultorum'', marketed commercially as the '''wax begonia''', is a hybrid of at least five species, including ''B. cucullata''.{{cite journal |last1=Pounders |first1=Cecil T. |last2=Sakhanokho |first2=Hamidou F. |last3=Nyochembeng |first3=Leopold M. |title=Begonia ×semperflorens FB08-59 and FB08-163 Clonal Germplasm |journal=HortScience |date=January 2015 |volume=50 |issue=1 |pages=145–146 |doi=10.21273/HORTSCI.50.1.145 |doi-access=free}} The name ''wax begonia'' refers to the thick and waxy leaves of the group.{{cite web |title=Semperflorens (ever-blooming) |date=July 2021 |url=https://www.begonias.org/semperflorens-ever-blooming/ |publisher=American Begonia Society |access-date=8 May 2022}} According to [[Catalog of Life]] (February 6, 2017) 6 and Kew Garden World Checklist, these varieties exist:[https://florafaunaweb.nparks.gov.sg/special-pages/plant-detail.aspx?id=5285 Begonia cucullata Willd.]{{cite web |url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/annual-checklist/2014/details/species/id/11783285 |title=Species 2000 & ITIS Catalogue of Life: 2014 Annual Checklist. |author=Roskov Y. |author2=Kunze T. |author3=Orrell T. |author4=Abucay L. |author5=Paglinawan L. |author6=Culham A. |author7=Bailly N. |author8=Kirk P. |author9=Bourgoin T.|author10= Baillargeon G. |author11=Decock W. |author12=De Wever A. |editor=Didžiulis V. |year=2014 |publisher=Species 2000: Reading, UK. |access-date=May 26, 2014}} * ''Begonia cucullata'' var.
